newsitem.title: USA: Unimed shares off after president resigns.
newsitem.headline: Unimed shares off after president resigns.

text.p: Unimed Pharmaceuticals Inc shares dropped 1-3/8 to 6-1/2 after the company announced its president and chief executive officer, Stephen Simes, resigned to pursue other business interests.
Asked if the drop in the stock and the president's resignation were related, David Riggs, senior vice president of Unimed said, "I expect that they are. It was a surprise."
He added, however, that Unimed believes its outlook is "very bright."
"We have an excellent pipeline," Riggs said. "Nothing has changed with respect to developing that pipeline. The future of the company is very good, we believe."
Unimed develops and markets niche pharmaceutical products for AIDS, endocrinology and urology therapeutic areas. Its main product is Marinol for treating Alzheimer's disease.
Riggs said the company expects to begin a search immediately to fill the president's position on a permanent basis. "A number of individuals will be considered, including insiders," Riggs said.
No further details on Simes' resignation were available.
Earlier today, Unimed said Robert Dudley, vice president of clinical and regulatory affairs, was named interim president and chief executive officer.
